title: Day 18 — Cursor Pagination Off-by-One
prompt: Infinite scroll is showing a duplicate row at each page boundary, and the next cursor looks wrong. Here's the cursor pagination code. How do you debug it?

clarifications.answer: The cursor is the last id the client already saw, so the next page must be ids STRICTLY greater than the cursor — the duplicate is an off-by-one there.
next_cursor should be the LAST item's id in the returned page, not the first.
next_cursor is None when there are no items after this page.
Items are pre-sorted ascending by id — you can rely on that.
A cursor past the last id returns an empty page and a None cursor.
Trace ids [1..5], limit 2, cursor 2: the '>=' makes it return [2,3] instead of [3,4] — item 2 was already shown.

hints: Hand-trace two adjacent pages and watch which item repeats.
Start condition should be 'id > cursor' (strictly), not 'id >= cursor'.
next_cursor = page[-1].id only if items remain after this page (start+limit < len), else None.
